ImageDescription.value:
Kazakh shepard with dogs and horse.
I took this picture of a shepherd in Western Kazakhstan in Feb. 2004. I own the picture. This man lives in the steppe south of Aktobinsk, western Kazakhstan. He lives in a small farm house with electricity but no water. He owns quite a few goats and sheep and 2 camels that I know of. He was very happy to have his picture taken. In February 2004 when I took this picture he was on his horse watching over his herd and was most likely going to spend the day sitting on his horse like this. We were driving by on our way to Aktobinsk and he left his herd for a while to come and talk to us. He carries a gun to kill any wolf who tries to get to his herd, a common problem in that area.

ImageDescription.value: Recently shot sled dog in Upernavik, Greenland. The stock of sled dogs in Upernavik are regulated by shooting. A dog shooter is hired for the regulation - the dog is killed on-site by a rifle shot in the head in the open terrain. Afterwards the dog is drawn to a road side, whereafter it is refuse collected. This particular dog was photographed shortly after the shot was fired at a road side. The sled dog stock in Upernavik is decreasing these years. In the last few winters rising temperatures and changed currents in the sea around the island have made it impossible to use sled dogs for hunting and transportation.

Artistically designed front door “Rua de Santa Maria 27” (Claire Micklin, The arT of oPEn doORs), Funchal, Madeira, Portugal
The project “artE das pORtas Abertas” in Rua de Santa Maria and its side streets in Funchal is an art project by various artists that aims to open doors to art and culture. These art interventions take into account all visual arts, from painting and photography to writing.
The project was initiated by artist José Maria Montero Zyberchema and former Regional Secretary for Tourism and Culture João Carlos Abreu. The first door to undergo an intervention was number 207 on Rua de Carreira in Funchal by Martinho Mendes on August 20, 2010. The first door in Rua Santa Maria was painted on April 6, 2011, by artist Mark Milewski at number 77, which took him more than a month to complete. However, the first artistic intervention was started and completed by Gonçalo Martins in Rua Santa Maria nos. 81 to 83 on April 9, 2011.
